searchText: Re EIP-2935, am I understanding correctly that even though the account is empty (balance 0, nonce 0, no code) it should be inserted into the database and be part of state root calc? that’s the idea, SSTORE, SLOAD the data https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/v1.5.0-alpha.0/tests/formats/operations states that there should be a `<input-name>.ssz_snappy` for each test, but https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-spec-tests/tree/v1.5.0-alpha.0/tests/minimal/electra/operations/consolidation/pyspec_tests/multiple_consolidations_below_churn https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-spec-tests/tree/v1.5.0-alpha.0/tests/minimal/electra/operations/consolidation/pyspec_tests/multiple_consolidations_equal_churn https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-spec-tests/tree/v1.5.0-alpha.0/tests/minimal/electra/operations/consolidation/pyspec_tests/multiple_consolidations_equal_twice_churn etc only have `pre`/`post` states? The test vector is wrong (missing operation). I will fix it. Thank you for reporting it! <holiman> > <holiman> It would be touch-deleted later tho.. ? (re @amphora_interop_bot: <nordbjerg> Re EIP-2935, am I understanding correctly that even though the account is empty (balance 0, nonce 0, no code) it should be inserted into the database and be part of state root calc?) let me rephrase the account is empty according to EIP-161 (no code, zero nonce, zero balance), so according to that EIP the account should not exist. is the account in EIP-2935 exempt from this? this <holiman> That would make zero sense (special-casing it like that). Better to give it a nonce or 1-wei balance and let the rules remain, imo It wasn't defined explicitly before, but in 7002 the withdrawal requests should appear in the requests lists in the same order they are dequeued (h/t <@508125616940515329> . I made a PR adding this text to the spec: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/8502 Would it make sense to add an `id` field to the withdrawal request encoding? It is now assumed that the list which gets outputted from the EVM for the operations is now in the "right order" for the withdrawals. If an `id` field is added this is made more explicit (but of course leads to more bandwith, and this also does not feel necessary) 🤔 I would be able to sort an arbitrary array with withdrawals in it, however I cannot be sure that the withdrawals operations are in the right order given an arbitrary list 🤔 In EIP 6110 is the Request Type `0x00` (so 1 zero-byte) or `0x` (no bytes)? excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <holiman> That would make zero sense (special-casing it like that). Better to give it a nonce or 1-wei balance and let the rules remain, imo

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: It wasn't defined explicitly before, but in 7002 the withdrawal requests should appear in the requests lists in the same order they are dequeued (h/t <@508125616940515329> . I made a PR adding this text to the spec: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/8502

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Would it make sense to add an `id` field to the withdrawal request encoding? It is now assumed that the list which gets outputted from the EVM for the operations is now in the "right order" for the withdrawals. If an `id` field is added this is made more explicit (but of course leads to more bandwith, and this also does not feel necessary) 🤔

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: I would be able to sort an arbitrary array with withdrawals in it, however I cannot be sure that the withdrawals operations are in the right order given an arbitrary list 🤔

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: In EIP 6110 is the Request Type `0x00` (so 1 zero-byte) or `0x` (no bytes)?
